rationale: The student includes the starting number when counting back (e.g., counting '12, 11, 10' for 3 hops instead of moving first to 11). A number-line subtract model explicitly draws each movement arc between numbers, showing that the first count happens after the first hop.

script.focus: the first hop moving to 13 before counting 1

intent: Demonstrate subtract on the number-line with values [14,3]. Tutor points at: the first hop moving to 13 before counting 1

content.title: Counting back, one hop at a time

frames.caption: Start at 14. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet.
Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.

judgement.reasoning: The demonstration directly addresses the exact misconception ('Start at 14. We have not hopped yet. Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started'). It uses a different problem (14 - 3 instead of 12 - 3) so it does not leak the answer, uses the same number line tool with clear captions/visual hops, and lowers cognitive load as a worked example.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this worked demonstration clearly models not counting the starting number before hopping, directly clearing up the student's specific error.
